app.title: Still More to Know
app.subtitle: 36 questions for people who already know each other

startScreen.title: Still More to Know
description: Take turns and listen before responding.
Either person can pass without explaining.

endScreen.title: Familiar, Not Finished
endScreen.subtitle: Knowing someone is something you keep doing.

now.name: Who We Are Now
now.description: The inner life that may have changed since you last asked

friction.name: What We Avoid
friction.description: Needs, defenses, and tensions hidden by familiarity

choose.name: What We Choose Next
choose.description: Appreciation, repair, and the relationship you want to keep making

questions.question: What has changed in you recently that I may not have noticed?
more: When did you first notice it yourself?
How would you like me to respond to that change?

questions.question: What is taking up more of your inner life than it appears from the outside?
more: What part of it is hardest to explain?

questions.question: What ordinary habit is quietly keeping you afloat right now?
more: How could I make more room for it?

questions.question: What are you postponing while calling it bad timing?
more: What are you waiting to feel before you begin?
What if that feeling never arrives?

questions.question: Where are you calling fear being realistic?
more: What is the realistic risk?
What part of the answer is only fear?

questions.question: When have you felt most like yourself lately?
more: Who were you with?
What were you not having to manage?

questions.question: What are you learning to ask for more directly?
more: What made asking feel difficult before?

questions.question: What makes you defensive because some part of it might be true?
more: Separate the unfair part from the useful part.

questions.question: What do you envy lately, and what desire might it be pointing toward?
more: Keep the desire. Remove the person you compare yourself with.

questions.question: What have you made part of your personality because changing it would be inconvenient?
more: Who might you be without that explanation?

questions.question: Each choose one recent photo that says: This is where I am now.
more: Explain what the image cannot show.
Ask one question before sharing your own photo.

questions.question: Write one assumption you have been making about the other person's life. Compare.
more: Do not defend the assumption.
Let the other person replace it with something more accurate.

questions.question: What do I do that makes it easier for you to be honest?
more: Name a specific moment, not a general quality.

questions.question: What do I do that makes honesty feel expensive?
more: Describe the effect before judging the intention.
What would lower the cost?

questions.question: What recurring disagreement might be the safer version of a deeper one?
more: What deeper subject keeps getting translated into the smaller argument?

questions.question: Where do you ask me for honesty but reward me for keeping you comfortable?
more: What response from you would make the truth safer?

questions.question: What need have you been hoping I would notice without being told?
more: Ask for it now in one clear sentence.

questions.question: Which boundary do you usually mention only after it has been crossed?
more: What stops you from naming it earlier?
How can I recognize it sooner?

questions.question: What have you forgiven in words but still carry in your behavior?
more: What would repair look like beyond another apology?

questions.question: What role do you think you keep playing in our relationship?
more: When is that role useful?
When does it become a trap?

questions.question: When do you feel managed by me instead of met by me?
more: What would being met look like in the same situation?

questions.question: What truth would you like me to hear without immediately fixing it?
more: Tell me what kind of response you want before you share.

questions.question: One person speaks for one minute. The other reflects what they heard before replying.
more: Use: What I hear matters most is...
The speaker may correct the reflection.

questions.question: Finish: I protect this relationship by..., but the cost is...
more: Both people answer.
Do not reassure each other until both answers are complete.

questions.question: What ordinary thing between us would you be genuinely sad to lose?
more: What keeps that small thing alive?

questions.question: What is one way I have changed you for the better without trying to?
more: When did you first see that change?

questions.question: What risk would feel easier if you knew I was beside you?
more: What kind of support would actually help?

questions.question: What apology are we using as a substitute for change?
more: What repeated behavior would need to become different?

questions.question: What appreciation do you need to hear more specifically?
more: Give the other person an example of language that would feel real.

questions.question: Where have we helped each other become braver?
more: What did the other person do besides encourage you?

questions.question: Which difference between us no longer needs to be solved?
more: What becomes possible when neither person has to win?

questions.question: What promise do we keep making with no system for keeping it?
more: Turn the promise into one visible behavior.

questions.question: If nothing between us changed for a year, what would disappoint you most?
more: What could each person change without waiting for the other?

questions.question: What should we stop pretending does not matter?
more: Name it without arguing the case yet.
Decide when to return to it properly.

questions.question: Plan one ordinary hour together that would make the next week feel better.
more: Keep it small enough to happen.
Choose when before moving on.

questions.question: Offer one truth you want to carry forward and one gratitude you do not want to leave unsaid.
more: The listener only receives it.
End by naming the next conversation, if one is needed.
